paragraph: Farideh’s mother had been asking her to stop at her aunt’s in Taft for three Thursdays, and each Thursday Farideh had driven back to Yazd with some small reason not to. This time her mother said only, “Bagh-e Golestan,” as if the neighbourhood itself could settle the matter, then added Sadri Garden because Farideh had once pretended not to know which place she meant. Farideh knew. When she reached Taft she slowed and kept going. Her aunt called before she had gone much farther. Farideh watched the name disappear from the screen, pulled over, and called her mother instead. “I’m here,” she said. Her mother asked, “At her house?” Farideh looked back the way she had come. “In Taft.” Neither of them spoke for a moment. Then Farideh put the car into gear and turned around.
